FAQ

1
What are insulated rock wool / mineral fireproof sandwich roof wall panels?
Insulated rock wool / mineral fireproof sandwich roof wall panels are building cladding materials made from a combination of rock wool or mineral wool insulation sandwiched between two layers of metal or cement boards.
2
How are these panels used in prefabricated building wall cladding?
These panels are used as exterior wall cladding in prefabricated buildings to provide insulation, fire resistance, and structural support. They serve as a protective barrier against external elements and help maintain a comfortable indoor environment.
3
What are the advantages of using insulated rock wool / mineral fireproof sandwich roof wall panels?
These panels offer several advantages, including excellent thermal insulation properties, high fire resistance, sound absorption, and durability. They are also lightweight, easy to install, and can be customized to suit various architectural designs.
4
In which scenarios can these panels be applied?
Insulated rock wool / mineral fireproof sandwich roof wall panels find application in a wide range of scenarios, including commercial buildings, industrial facilities, residential construction, warehouses, agricultural structures, and cold storage facilities. They are particularly suitable for buildings located in areas with extreme weather conditions or high fire risk.
5
How do these panels contribute to energy efficiency?
The excellent thermal insulation properties of insulated rock wool / mineral fireproof sandwich roof wall panels help to reduce heat transfer through the building envelope, thereby improving energy efficiency. By minimizing heat loss or gain, these panels can lead to lower heating and cooling costs for the building owners.
6
Are these panels eco-friendly?
Yes, these panels are considered eco-friendly. The rock wool or mineral wool insulation material used is typically made from natural and recyclable materials. Additionally, the long lifespan and high durability of these panels contribute to reducing overall waste generation in the construction industry.
